title: Marine wildlife fleeing to poles due to global heating as Australian oceans face ‘uncharted’ future
summary: From 2040 onwards the average year for marine ecosystems is likely to be more extreme than the worst years experienced up until 2015, researchers say Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here Australia’s oceans will enter “uncharted territory” by 2040 due to global heating, even if significant emissions cuts occur, new research has found. Australian researchers modelled ocean conditions under four scenarios, including current, high- and low-emissions futures. They found that in 15 years, marine ecosystems would be facing extreme heat, oxygen loss and acidity conditions.
